credentials.description: Notch Pay private key, sent as is in Authorization and in X-Grant, for transfers, beneficiaries, balance and webhooks

example_prompt: Delete a Notch Pay beneficiary by ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique beneficiary ID to delete.

gotchas: Authorization takes the key as is, with no 'Bearer ' prefix. Which key goes there is unsettled: Notch Pay's Authentication page shows the public key in it next to X-Grant (`-H "Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY"` `-H "X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY"`), while this spec sends the private key, following its earlier note that a public key returns 406 Not Acceptable (not stated in the docs). See open_questions before relying on either.
Deletion is permanent and irreversible. There is no archive or soft-delete — once deleted, the beneficiary ID cannot be recovered.
A 404 response means either the beneficiary does not exist or it belongs to a different API key. Beneficiaries are scoped to the account that created them.
Do not URL-encode the beneficiary ID when inserting it into the path — pass it as-is.

This endpoint also requires the `X-Grant` header carrying your private key (`X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY`). Without it Notch Pay returns 403 "This endpoint requires additional authentication"; a wrong value returns 403 "Invalid grant key".
open_questions: Notch Pay's docs show `Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY` together with `X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY` on this endpoint, while this spec sends the private key in Authorization (see the gotcha about 406 with a public key). Which key Authorization must carry when X-Grant is present is not confirmed.
